claim: The documented label-splitting rule (split at every non-alphanumeric character, at lowercase-to-uppercase changes, at the end of an uppercase run followed by lowercase, and between letters and digits; entries split the same way; match when the label's words contain all of an entry's words consecutively and in order, each word optionally carrying a trailing `s` or `es`) is the rule the code implements.
source_excerpt: **How labels match.** SQL Lens splits a column label into words at every character that is not a letter or digit, at lowercase-to-uppercase changes, at the end of an uppercase run followed by lowercase letters, and between letters and digits (`password_hash` → password, hash; `APIKey` → api, key; `password2` → password, 2). Entries split the same way. A label matches when its words contain all of an entry's words, consecutively and in order; each word may also carry a trailing `s` or `es` (`api_keys`, `PINs`).
